 Live Updates Updated Thu, Oct 22 2026 8:11 PM EDT Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Stock futures are little changed after tech sector sell-off: Live updates
 Lee Ying Shan Tobias Burns A trader works at the New York Stock Exchange on Oct. 21, 2026. NYSE U.S. equity futures were about flat on Thursday evening after tech stocks sold off on concerns that the artificial intelligence trade may be faltering, at least for the near term.
 Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 52 points, or 0.1%. S&P 500 futures gained 0.06%, and Nasdaq-100 futures slipped 0.1%.
 In regular trading, the S&P 500 sank 1.2%, and the Nasdaq Composite slid 2.6%. The broad market benchmark posted its worst session since July, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq had its worst day since June. The Dow Industrials bucked the trend and closed marginally higher.
 In Asia, South Korea's benchmark Kospi Index fell 2.42%, while Japan's  Nikkei 225  lost 0.49%. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was 0.21% lower.
 Worries around artificial intelligence spending weighed down the market and dragged the U.S. tech sector to a 3% decline on the day. Nvidia dropped 4.4%, Alphabet fell 3.2%, and Advanced Micro Devices declined 8.1% as losses occurred in different parts of the technology sector.
 Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told CNBC on Thursday he thought capital within the AI buildout was becoming scarce.
 "There's a scarcity of capital. The demand [for] the capital is much greater than the availability of the capital," Huang said when asked about the neocloud segment of the AI buildout, which is proving to be fragile.
 Ed Yardeni, president of Yardeni Research, described the AI trade on Thursday as a "bubble" but said that some depressurization wouldn't be all bad.
 "Taking some air out of the AI bubble is a good thing. I don't think it's going to burst and create problems for the economy," he said, pointing to the bond market as a source of capital competition for equities.
 Bond yields eased on Thursday, with the 10-year Treasury sliding 18.5 basis points to 4.961% as traders bid up safe-haven assets. The yield on the 30-year slid 15 basis points, and the 2-year yield fell 17.5 basis points.
 Brent crude prices spiked following a report that the U.S. and Israel were drawing up plans for renewed attacks on Iran as part of the regional war that started in late February. Brent jumped 4% to end the session at $113.17, the highest settle since May .
 On the week, the S&P 500 is heading for a slim gain, up less than 0.1%, while the Nasdaq is down 0.5% in the period. The Dow is tracking for a 1.7% advance.
 On the economic front, traders will be watching for the final reading of the University of Michigan's consumer sentiment report.
 59 Min Ago South Korea stocks lead declines as Asia markets open lower
 Asia-Pacific markets fell on Friday, with South Korean equities leading declines in the region.
 The benchmark Kospi index fell 2.42%, while the tech-heavy Kosdaq index declined 2.6%.
 Japan's  Nikkei 225  lost 0.49% and the broader Topix declined 0.86%.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was 0.21% lower.
 —Lee Ying Shan 
 2 Hours Ago Asia-Pacific markets set to fall, tracking Wall Street losses on AI concerns
 Asia-Pacific markets were set to mostly fall on Friday, tracking losses on Wall Street as concerns over soaring artificial intelligence spending and surging oil prices weighed on investor sentiment.
 Futures for Japan's  Nikkei 225  in Chicago were at 62,360 while in Osaka they were last at 62,310 compared with the index's previous close of 62,907.84.
 Futures for Hong Kong's Hang Seng index last traded at 23,133, compared with the index's last close of 22,934.68.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was down 0.34% in early trading.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 3 Hours Ago Stocks making the biggest moves in after hours: Western Digital, Bloom Energy & more
 Several stocks saw dramatic swings in extended trading following another raft of quarterly reports.
 Western Digital — Shares of the data storage company fell 5%. The decline came after hard selling in the artificial intelligence trade during the regular session. Separately, Western Digital posted fiscal first quarter results that exceeded estimates, with adjusted earnings of $4.64 per share trouncing the LSEG consensus call for $4.09 per share. Revenue of $4.38 billion beat the expected $4.14 billion. 
 Bloom Energy — The fuel cell power company fell 5% even as third-quarter results trounced analysts' estimates. Adjusted earnings of 94 cents per share and revenue of $1.24 billion surpassed the LSEG consensus call for 68 cents per share and $1.06 billion. Guidance for full-year revenues and adjusted earnings also came in ahead of estimates.
 Read more about Thursday's big movers in extended trading here .
 — Darla Mercado 
 3 Hours Ago Sliding bond yields Thursday lift homebuilders, banks and REITs
 The largest one-day decline since March 2023 in the 10-year Treasury note yield Thursday helped drive up the value of homebuilders, banks and real estate investment trusts. 
 The State Street SPDR S&P Homebuilders ETF surged 3.8%, the State Street SPDR S&P Regional Banking ETF rallied 2.5% and the Vanguard Real Estate ETF added 1.3% — all of them handily outperforming the S&P 500, which dropped 1.2%.
 — Scott Schnipper 
 3 Hours Ago U.S. stock futures open little changed after tech rout
 U.S. stock futures were little changed as trading began at 6 p.m. in New York.
 Dow futures advanced 38 points, or 0.07%, while S&P 500 futures gained 0.05%. Nasdaq-100 futures slipped 0.07%.
 — Darla Mercado
